doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Jack Teagarden and why he stopped playing trombone
summary: Hearing Teagarden convinced him he had met his match; he saw Teagarden in 1957 with Earl Hines.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well that’s the reason I stopped playing the trombone. I heard Jack Teagarden. I’d got over my Kid Ory phase. I could do a bit of that. And then I heard this man Teagarden and what he was doing with the trombone and I think I realized that I’d met my match. The moment had passed you know. Fabulous. Fabulous player. Saw him once. Saw him in ’57. He came over with a super band led by Earl Hines with Max Kaminsky and Cozy Cole on drums, and Jack Lesberg was playing the bass. That was in ’57. And we saw Teagarden play that amazing thing where he takes the bell of the instrument off and he puts the water glass over the end of the slide and just plays the slide. You know? Takes the bell of the instrument away, puts the water glass over the bit of piping that would have been connected to the bell and just plays the slide.
It’s a fabulous sound. I saw him do that. I can always remember that.
